name: How do I choose tile for a small guest bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What tile size, finish, and pattern work best in a small guest bathroom without overwhelming the room?
mainEntity.text: What tile size, finish, and pattern work best in a small guest bathroom without overwhelming the room?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a small guest bathroom, tile should help the room feel calm, durable, and easy to clean. Large-format tile is often a strong choice because it reduces grout lines and can make the space feel more open. On floors, slip resistance matters just as much as style, especially in a bathroom that guests may use only occasionally. On the walls, a simple pattern or a restrained accent usually works better than several competing materials. The best tile choice also depends on maintenance. Light grout can look great at first but may require more upkeep, while heavily textured tile can be harder to clean. A guest bath should look polished without feeling overly busy. In many Los Angeles homes, the most successful designs use a few durable materials and repeat them consistently rather than changing finishes at every surface.
acceptedAnswer.description: Large-format tile often works well in small guest bathrooms because it reduces grout lines and makes the space feel cleaner. Choose slip-resistant flooring, limit busy patterns, and use tile colors that coordinate with the vanity and wall finish. The tile should suit both style and maintenance needs.
